question.text: Regulation 91(B) of SEBI LODR Regulations maps the applicable disclosure regime for a For-Profit Enterprise whose designated securities are listed on the stock exchange(s). The regulation provides that:

answer.text: All FPEs listed on SSE follow a uniform disclosure code irrespective of Main Board / SME / IGP segment.
FPEs are exempted from normal LODR disclosures once they register on SSE.

FPEs shall comply with the disclosure requirements applicable to issuers whose specified securities are listed on the Main Board or the SME Exchange or the Innovators Growth Platform, as the case may be.
FPEs must comply with NPO-specific 91(C) disclosures in addition to main-board LODR.

explanation.text: The Logic: Reg 91(B) mandates segment-linked compliance: the FPE follows the disclosure regime of the platform on which its specified securities are actually listed - Main Board, SME Exchange or IGP. The SSE layer sits in addition. A 'uniform SSE code' (A) or NPO-code application (D) or general exemption (C) would conflict with 91(B). The Trap: Candidates sometimes assume SSE registration simplifies disclosures; actually it adds to them. The answer hinges on the phrase 'as the case may be' - segment-specific application. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/III-C tests Main Board / SME / IGP regime differences; XXIII's 91(B) points the reader back to whichever segment regime applies. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When accepting an AIR engagement for a dual-listed FPE, demand the client's compliance calendar for its main-board / SME / IGP listing. The SIA cannot sign Form 3.1 if the underlying entity is delinquent on its parent-segment LODR obligations.
